title: Engagement Memory and Casebook
goal: Persist non-secret engagement memory across runs so the AI can reuse discovered architecture, prior blocked paths, accepted gaps, resolved findings, target context, and customer constraints without storing credentials or private runtime material.
scope: AI memory, engagement continuity, and evidence-linked casebook summaries.
generation_reason: A strong AI pentest platform should learn from prior evidence in an engagement instead of starting every run as a blank tool sequence.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Memory must be non-secret, evidence-linked, tenant-bound, and must not broaden scope or persist credential material.

success_criteria: A casebook service records evidence-linked architecture notes, blocked paths, accepted gaps, resolved findings, and operator constraints.
AI planning can read casebook memory with tenant and engagement boundaries.
Credential values, tokens, cookies, and secret material are never stored in the casebook.

acceptance_criteria: Casebook entries are evidence-linked and tenant-isolated.
Secret-like values are redacted or rejected.
AI planner uses casebook context only as planning input, not as proof.

after_completion: Promote exactly one next task into NEXT_TASK.md.

out_of_scope: Using memory as evidence without source IDs
